notes_for_editor: Thin record: an NGS datasheet with a 1952 first-observed date and a lookout-tower marker code, plus the FFLA 'Tower Gone' entry. The centraluslookouts page gives the same NGS datasheet with no description. A YouTube video titled 'A Forgotten Chapter of Sam Houston National Forest' and a search snippet say 'around 1950' for the Four Notch tower; the page fetched returned only its title, so that date is unverified and not used. A Lone Star Hiking Trail group post mentions a Four Notch Hunter Camp in the Sam Houston National Forest; it concerns a camp, not verified as the tower site, and is not used. The 1952 date is a survey observation, not a construction date. NGS NAD83 coordinates (30 38 45.37 N, 095 25 24.45 W) match the record within about 10 m. A USFS catalog photo titled 'Fournotch - Sam Houston National Forest' (1980, CC BY-ND 4.0, https://scholarworks.sfasu.edu/nfgt_general/293/) is not added as a photo: the record does not say it shows the tower, and the image was not checked. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story no longer says Four Notch was part of a Forest Service network. No source read ties this station to that program, and the Texas column (which does not name Four Notch) is cited only as background.
